  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>CONNECTONE BANCORP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES </b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS </b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>(unaudited)</b></p>

    &#160;

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:OrganizationConsolidationAndPresentationOfFinancialStatementsDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3175134" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><b><a id="notes" title="notes" href="#"></a>Note <em style="font: inherit;">1a.</em></b><b>&#160;Nature of Operations, Principles of Consolidation and Risk and Uncertainties</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="cnob:NatureOfOperationsPolicyTextBlock" id="c144280451" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Nature of Operations</span></i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">ConnectOne Bancorp, Inc. (the &#8220;Parent Corporation&#8221;) is incorporated under the laws of the State of New Jersey and is a registered bank holding company under the Bank Holding Company Act of <em style="font: inherit;">1956,</em> as amended (the &#8220;BHCA&#8221;). The Parent Corporation&#8217;s business currently consists of the operation of its wholly-owned subsidiary, ConnectOne Bank (the &#8220;Bank&#8221; and, collectively with the Parent Corporation and the Parent Corporation&#8217;s subsidiaries, the &#8220;Company&#8221;) and making certain limited investments. The Bank&#8217;s direct and indirect subsidiaries include Union Investment Co. (a New Jersey investment company), Twin Bridge Investment Co. (a Delaware&#160;investment company), ConnectOne Preferred Funding Corp. (a New Jersey real estate investment trust), Center Financial Group, LLC (a New Jersey financial services company), Center Advertising, Inc. (a New Jersey advertising company), Morris Property Company, LLC, (a New Jersey limited liability company), Volosin Holdings, LLC, (a New Jersey limited liability company), NJCB Spec-<em style="font: inherit;">1,</em> LLC (a New Jersey limited liability company), Port Jervis Holdings, LLC (a New Jersey&#160;limited liability company), BONJ Special Properties, LLC (a New Jersey limited liability company),&#160;The First of Long Island REIT (a New York real estate investment trust), FNY Service Corp (a New York investment company) and BoeFly, Inc. (a New Jersey financial technology company).</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Bank is a community-based, full-service New Jersey-chartered commercial bank that was founded in <em style="font: inherit;">2005.</em> The Bank operates from its headquarters located at <em style="font: inherit;">301</em> Sylvan Avenue in the Borough of Englewood Cliffs, Bergen County, New Jersey and through its&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">55</em>&#160;other banking offices located in New Jersey, New York and Florida. On <em style="font: inherit;"> June 1, 2025, </em>the Company completed its acquisition of The First of Long Island Corporation (&#8220;FLIC&#8221;), and The First National Bank of Long Island ("FNBLI"), FLIC&#8217;s wholly owned subsidiary depository institution, was merged into the Bank. See Note <em style="font: inherit;">2.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Substantially all loans are secured with various types of collateral, including business assets, consumer assets and commercial/residential real estate. Each borrower&#8217;s ability to repay their&#160;loans is dependent on the conversion of assets, cash flows generated from the borrowers&#8217; business, real estate rental and consumer wages.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c144280452" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Basis of Presentation and Principles&#160;of Consolidation</span></i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The consolidated financial statements have been prepared in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles ("GAAP"). The consolidated financial statements of the Parent Corporation are prepared on an accrual basis and include the accounts of the Parent Corporation and the Bank. All significant intercompany accounts and transactions have been eliminated from the accompanying consolidated financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b></b></p><ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>CONNECTONE BANCORP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES </b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS </b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>(unaudited)</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;&#160; &#160;&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">1a.</em></b><b>&#160;Nature of Operations, Principles of Consolidation and Risk and Uncertainties - (continued)</b></p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 16pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 16pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c144280453" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 16pt;"><b><i>Segment Reporting</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company&#8217;s operations are solely in the financial services industry, providing a range of regional community banking services to commercial and retail clients.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company's reportable segment is determined by the Chief Executive&#160;Officer, who is designated the Chief Operating Decision Maker ("CODM"), based upon information about the Company's products and services offered, primarily its banking operations. The segment is also distinguished by the level of information provided to the CODM, who uses such information to&#160;review performance of&#160;various components of the business (such as branches and the subsidiary bank), which are then aggregated if operating performance, products/services, and customers are similar. The CODM&#160;will evaluate the financial performance of the Company's business components such as by evaluating revenue streams, significant expenses, and budget to actual results in assessing the Company's segment and in the determination of allocating resources. The CODM&#160;uses revenue streams to evaluate product pricing and significant expenses to assess performance and evaluate return on assets. The CODM&#160;uses consolidated net income to benchmark the Company&#160;against its competitors. The benchmarking analysis coupled with monitoring of budget to actual results are used in assessment of performance and in establishing compensation. Loans, investments, and deposits provide the revenues in the banking operation. Interest expense, provision for credit losses, and payroll provide the significant expenses in the banking operation. All operations are domestic.&#160;See Note <em style="font: inherit;">14</em> for disclosures related to the reportable segment.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 9pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 9pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:PostemploymentBenefitPlansPolicy" id="c144280454" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 9pt;"><b><i>Employee Benefit Plans</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160; &#160; &#160; &#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company has a noncontributory pension plan that covered all eligible employees up until&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2007</em><i>,</i>&#160;at which time the Company froze its defined benefit pension plan. As such, all future benefit accruals in this pension plan were discontinued and all retirement benefits that employees would have earned as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2007&#160;</em>were preserved.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In the FLIC merger, the Company acquired a defined benefit pension plan that covered all former eligible FLIC employees. Prior to the freezing of the Plan the Bank made contributions to the plan, which together with participant contributions equal to <ix:nonFraction id="c144274575" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanEmployerMatchingContributionPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">2</ix:nonFraction>% of their compensation, fund these benefits.&#160;Effective <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025, </em>the plan was frozen and all retirement benefits that employees earned through that date were preserved.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 7pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company&#8217;s policy is to fund at least the minimum contribution required by the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of&#160;<i><em style="font: inherit;">1974.</em></i>&#160;Pension expense is the sum of service cost, interest cost, amortization of actuarial gains and losses and plan expenses, net of the expected return on plan assets and participant contributions. The costs associated with the plans are accrued based on actuarial assumptions and included in deposit, loan and other income.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company accounts for its defined benefit pension plans in accordance with&#160;Financial Accounting Standards Board ("FASB") Accounting Standard Codification ("ASC")&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">715</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">30</em><i>.</i>&#160;This standard requires that the funded status of defined benefit postretirement plans be recognized on the Company&#8217;s statement of financial condition and changes in the funded status be reflected in other comprehensive income ("OCI"). This standard also requires companies to measure the funded status of the plans as of the date of the company's fiscal year-end.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 16pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 16pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 16pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:UseOfEstimates" id="c144280455" escape="true"><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 16pt;"><b><i>Use of Estimates</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In preparing the consolidated financial statements, management has made estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities as of the dates of the consolidated statements of condition and that affect the results of operations for the periods presented. Actual results could differ significantly from those estimates.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 16pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 16pt;"><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:PriorPeriodReclassificationAdjustmentDescription" id="c144280456" escape="true"><p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 16pt;"><i><b>Reclassifications</b></i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Certain reclassifications have been made to amounts reported in prior periods to conform to the current period presentation. The reclassifications had <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> material effect on net income or total stockholders' equity.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><b style="font-size: 10pt;"></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c144280457" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><b style="font-size: 10pt;">Note <em style="font: inherit;">1b.</em> Authoritative Accounting Guidance</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b><i><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Newly Issued, But</span></i></b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">&#160;<b><i><em style="font: inherit;">Not</em></i></b>&#160;<b><i>Yet Effective Accounting Standards</i></b></span></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024, </em>the FASB issued ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03,</em> "Income Statement - Reporting Comprehensive Income - Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic <em style="font: inherit;">220</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40</em>)" ("ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03"</em>). ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em> requires public entities to provide disaggregated disclosures, in the notes to the financial statements, of certain categories of expenses that are included in expense line items on the face of the income statement. ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03</em> is effective for the Company on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2027.&#160;</em>The Company is currently <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expecting the ASU to have a material effect on the consolidated financial statements and footnotes.</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b></b></p><ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>CONNECTONE BANCORP, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES </b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS </b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>(unaudited)</b></p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b></b></p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3175135" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">2.</em></b>&#160;<b>Business Combination&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 36pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> June 1, 2025 (</em>the &#8220;Acquisition Date&#8221;), the Company completed the acquisition of FLIC, the parent company for the FNBLI, in accordance with the definitive Agreement and Plan of Merger dated as of <em style="font: inherit;"> September 4, 2024 (</em>the &#8220;Merger Agreement&#8221;).&#160;Pursuant to the Merger Agreement, on the Acquisition Date, FLIC merged with and into the Company, with the Company continuing as the surviving corporation, and FNBLI merged with and into the Bank, with the Bank as the surviving bank (collectively, the &#8220;merger&#8221;). As part of this merger, the Company acquired <em style="font: inherit;">36</em>&#160;branch offices located in Nassau and Suffolk Counties of Long Island, and the boroughs of New York City.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In connection with the completion of the merger, former FLIC shareholders received&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c144274605" contextRef="i_2025-06-01_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember" unitRef="Pure" name="cnob:BusinessAcquisitionEquityInterestIssuedOrIssuableShareExchangeRatio" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">0.5175</ix:nonFraction> shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock for each share of FLIC common stock they held. The value of the total transaction consideration was approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c144274606" contextRef="d_2025-06-01_2025-06-01_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationConsiderationTransferred1" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">270.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. The consideration included the issuance of&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c144274607" contextRef="d_2025-06-01_2025-06-01_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:BusinessAcquisitionEquityInterestsIssuedOrIssuableNumberOfSharesIssued" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">11,790,116</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock, valued at $<ix:nonFraction id="c144274608" contextRef="i_2025-05-30" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:SharePrice" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">22.97</ix:nonFraction> per share, which was the closing price of the Company&#8217;s common stock on <em style="font: inherit;"> May 30, 2025, </em>the last trading day prior to the consummation of the merger. Also included in the total consideration was cash in lieu of any fractional shares, which was effectively settled upon closing.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 35pt;">The acquisition of FLIC was accounted for as a business combination using the acquisition method of accounting. Accordingly, assets acquired, liabilities assumed, and consideration paid were recorded at estimated fair values on the Acquisition Date. During the measurement period, the Company updated its assessment of the fair value of net assets acquired, resulting in a net increase of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144274609" contextRef="d_2025-07-01_2025-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:GoodwillPurchaseAccountingAdjustments" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">4.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million to goodwill from the amount originally reported as <em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2025. </em>This adjustment was primarily related to finalizing the assessment of deferred tax assets and Section <em style="font: inherit;">382</em> valuation allowances. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026, </em>total goodwill recorded from the merger is $<ix:nonFraction id="c144274611" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">11.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. This goodwill is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> amortizable or deductible for tax purposes and represents the future economic benefits and synergies expected from the combined operations.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">There have been <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> adjustments to the preliminary purchase price allocation during the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026. </em>While the measurement period remains open until <em style="font: inherit;"> June 1, 2026, </em>the Company&#8217;s valuation and assessment are substantially complete. The Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> anticipate any further material adjustments to the preliminary valuations before the expiration of the measurement period.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In connection with the acquisition, the consideration paid, and the fair value of identifiable assets acquired and liabilities assumed as of the Acquisition Date are summarized in the following tables:</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS </b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>(unaudited)</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">2.</em></b>&#160;<b>Business Combination </b>&#8211;<b> (continued)</b></p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The following is a description of the valuation methodologies used to estimate the fair values of significant assets and liabilities presented above.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><i>Cash and cash equivalents</i>&#160;&#8211; The carrying amount of these items is a reasonable estimate of their fair value based on the short-term nature of these assets.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><i>Investment securities</i>&#160;&#8211; Fair values for available-for-sale securities&#160;were based on quoted market prices, where available. If quoted market prices were <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available, fair value estimates are based on observable inputs, including quoted market prices for similar instruments. Fair value estimates also reflect an adjustment related to certain securities that were sold shortly after closing and were&#160;determined by the current market price. Additional information is included in Note <em style="font: inherit;">4</em> - Investments.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><i>Loans</i>&#160;&#8211; The fair value of the loan portfolio was calculated on a pooled loan basis using discounted cash flow analysis for accruing loans and on an individual basis for nonaccrual loans. This analysis took into consideration the contractual terms of the loans and assumptions related to the credit risk, expected lifetime losses, qualitative factors, collateral values, discount rates, and other liquidity considerations to estimate projected cash flows. The assumptions used in determining the fair value of the loan portfolio were considered reasonable from a market-participant viewpoint.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Acquired loans are classified into <em style="font: inherit;">two</em>&#160;categories: purchased credit deteriorated (&#8220;PCD&#8221;) and non-PCD loans. PCD loans are defined as a loan or group of loans that have experienced more-than-insignificant credit deterioration since origination. The Company considers various factors in connection with the identification of more-than-insignificant deterioration in credit, including but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> limited to nonperforming status, delinquency, risk ratings, and other qualitative factors that indicate deterioration in credit quality since origination. Non-PCD loans will have an allowance established subsequent to the Acquisition Date, which is recognized as an expense through the provision for credit losses. For PCD loans, the loans were recorded at their amortized cost, less an allowance for credit losses ("ACL") of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144274624" contextRef="i_2025-06-01_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember_CreditLossStatusAxis-FinancialAssetAcquiredWithCreditDeteriorationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLossExcludingAccruedInterest" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">43.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million on the Acquisition Date. There is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> provision for credit loss expense recognized on PCD loans because the initial allowance is established by grossing-up the amortized cost of the PCD loans. The remaining difference between the net of the amortized cost basis and the ACL&#160;and the fair value allocated to the loans on the date of acquisition is recognized as a non-credit-related discount that will be accreted into interest income over the life of the loans.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><i>Premises and equipment</i> &#8211; The estimated fair value of premises was&#160;measured based upon appraisals from independent <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> parties. The estimated fair value of equipment was determined to approximate the carrying amount of these assets.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><i>Deferred Tax Benefit</i> &#8211; The Company recorded a net deferred income tax benefit of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144274629" contextRef="d_2025-06-02_2025-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredIncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5" sign="-">46.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million related to the tax attributes of FLIC, along with the effects of fair value adjustments resulting from applying the purchase method of accounting. This amount represents a measurement period adjustment from the preliminary $<ix:nonFraction id="c144274630" contextRef="d_2025-06-01_2025-06-01_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredIncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5" sign="-">51.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million benefit previously reported. The current estimate reflects the $<ix:nonFraction id="c144274631" contextRef="d_2025-06-02_2025-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember" unitRef="USD" name="cnob:BusinessCombinationProvisionalInformationInitialAccountingIncompleteAdjustmentDeferredTaxAsset" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5" sign="-">4.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million net decrease in deferred tax assets described above, which accounts for the true-up of tax attributes, the application of the finalized <ix:nonFraction id="c144274632" contextRef="d_2025-06-02_2025-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember" unitRef="Pure" name="cnob:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationBlendedTaxRatePercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">30.9</ix:nonFraction>% blended statutory tax rate, and the recognition of a valuation allowance related to Section <em style="font: inherit;">382</em> limitations.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><em style="font: inherit;">No</em> changes were made to these estimates during the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026. </em>While the measurement period remains open until <em style="font: inherit;"> June 1, 2026, </em>the Company&#8217;s assessment of the combined statutory tax rates and the differences between the book and tax bases of acquired assets and assumed liabilities is substantially complete. Although these amounts remain preliminary until the expiration of the measurement period, the Company believes the current values reflect the final fair value of these attributes in all material respects and does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> anticipate further adjustments.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><i>Deposits</i> &#8211; The fair values used for the demand and savings deposits equal the amount payable on demand at the Acquisition Date. The fair value of time deposits is estimated by discounting the estimated future cash flows using current rates offered for deposits with similar remaining maturities.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><i>Borrowings</i> &#8211; The fair value of Federal Home Loan Bank ("FHLB") advances were estimated by discounting the estimated future cash flows using rates currently available to the Company for debt with similar remaining maturities.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>

These amounts were expensed as incurred and are recorded within "Merger Expenses and Restructuring Charges" in the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Statements of Income.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">4.</em></b>&#160;<b>Investment Securities</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">All of the Company&#8217;s investment securities were classified as available-for-sale as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025. </em>Available-for-sale securities are reported at fair value, with unrealized gains and losses, net of tax, included in accumulated other comprehensive income within stockholders&#8217; equity. Fair value is determined using quoted market prices or, in instances of limited market activity, based on various assumptions. See Note <em style="font: inherit;">7</em>&#160;of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements for further discussion regarding the valuation of the Company&#8217;s investment securities.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company has elected to exclude accrued interest from the amortized cost of its available-for-sale securities.&#160;Accrued interest receivable for available-for-sale securities totaled $<ix:nonFraction id="c144274804" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleAccruedInterestAfterAllowanceForCreditLoss" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">4.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c144274805" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleAccruedInterestAfterAllowanceForCreditLoss" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">5.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million&#160;as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">4.</em></b>&#160;<b>Investment Securities </b>&#8211;<b> (continued)</b></p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company evaluates securities in an unrealized loss position for impairment related to credit losses on at least a quarterly basis. Securities in unrealized loss positions are <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> assessed as to whether we intend to sell, or if it is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that we will be required to sell the security before recovery of its amortized cost basis. If <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> of the criteria is met, the security&#8217;s amortized cost basis is written down to fair value through current earnings. For securities that do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> meet these criteria, the Company evaluates whether the decline in fair value resulted from credit losses or other factors. If this assessment indicates that a credit loss exists, we compare the present value of cash flows expected to be collected from the security with the amortized cost basis of the security. If the present value of cash flows expected to be collected is less than the amortized cost basis for the security, a credit loss exists and an ACL&#160;is recorded, limited to the amount that the fair value of the security is less than its amortized cost basis. Unrealized losses on asset backed securities and state and municipal securities have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been recognized into income because the issuers are of high credit quality and&#160;we do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> intend to sell and it is likely that we will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be required to sell the securities prior to their anticipated recovery. The decline in fair value is largely due to changes in interest rates and other market conditions. The issuers continue to make timely principal and interest payments on the securities. Any impairment that has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been recorded through an ACL&#160;is recognized in OCI, net of applicable taxes. The&#160;Company has <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144274819"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144274828">not</span></span> recognized an ACL for available-for-sale securities as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Federal agency obligations, residential and commercial mortgage-backed pass-through securities are issued by U.S. Government agencies and U.S. Government sponsored enterprises. Although a government guarantee exists on these investments, these entities are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> legally backed by the full faith and credit of the federal government, and the current support they receive is subject to a cap as part of the agreement entered into in <em style="font: inherit;">2008.</em> Nonetheless, at this time we do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> foresee any set of circumstances in which the government would <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> fund its commitments on these investments as the issuers are an integral part of the U.S. housing market in providing liquidity and stability. Therefore, we concluded that a <em style="font: inherit;">zero</em>-allowance approach for these investment securities is appropriate.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:DerivativeInstrumentsAndHedgingActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3175147" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">5.</em> Derivatives&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">As part of our overall asset liability management strategy, the Company utilizes interest rate swaps to help manage its interest rate risk position.&#160;The notional amount of an interest rate swap does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> represent amounts exchanged by the parties.&#160;The exchange of cash flow is determined by reference to the notional amount and the other terms of the interest rate swap agreements. Derivative instruments are recognized on the balance sheet at their fair value. The Company&#8217;s cash flow hedges are reported on a gross basis as they are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> subject to master netting arrangements. Conversely, interest rate caps are reported on a net basis in the balance sheet, as these instruments are subject to enforceable master netting agreements that allow for the offsetting of assets and liabilities with the same counterparty.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><b>Derivatives Designated as Hedges</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Subsequent changes in fair value for a hedging instrument that has been designated and qualifies as part of a hedging relationship are accounted for in the following manner:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 88pt;"><em style="font: inherit;">1</em>) Cash flow hedges: changes in fair value are recognized as a component in OCI</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 88pt;"><em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) Fair value hedges: changes in fair value are recognized concurrently in earnings</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 81pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">As long as a hedging instrument is designated and the results of the effectiveness testing support that the instrument qualifies for hedge accounting treatment, <em style="font: inherit;">100%</em> of the periodic changes in fair value of the hedging instrument are accounted for as outlined above. This is the case whether or <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> economic mismatches exist in the hedging relationship. As a result, there is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> periodic measurement or recognition of ineffectiveness. Rather, the full impact of hedge gains and losses is recognized in the period in which the hedged transactions impact earnings. The change in fair value of the hedging instrument that is included in the assessment of hedge effectiveness is presented in the same income statement line item that is used to present the earnings effect of the hedged item.&#160;As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, the Bank was <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> utilizing fair value hedges.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: -9pt;"><b>Cash Flow Hedges</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company has&#160;entered into&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c144275115" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateSwapMember_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-CashFlowHedgingMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNumberOfInstrumentsHeld" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="INF">twelve</ix:nonFraction> pay fixed-rate interest rate swaps, with a total notional amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144275116" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateSwapMember_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-CashFlowHedgingMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeLiabilityNotionalAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">675</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million.&#160;These are designated as cash flow hedges of outstanding&#160;FHLB&#160;advances. We are required to pay fixed rates of interest ranging from <ix:nonFraction id="c144275117" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-CommencedFixedInterestRateSwapsMember_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-CashFlowHedgingMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DerivativeFixedInterestRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">0.63</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;to <ix:nonFraction id="c144275118" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-CommencedFixedInterestRateSwapsMember_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-CashFlowHedgingMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DerivativeFixedInterestRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">3.72</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;and receive variable rates of interest that reset quarterly based on the daily compounding secured overnight financing rate (&#8220;SOFR&#8221;).&#160;The swaps carry expiration dates ranging from&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> August 2026&#160;</em>to&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 2028.&#160;</em>The swaps are determined to be fully effective during the period presented and therefore&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;amount of ineffectiveness has been included in net income. Therefore, the aggregate fair value of the swap is recorded in other assets (liabilities) with changes in fair value recorded in other comprehensive income (loss) ("OCI"). The amount included in accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) ("AOCI")&#160;would be reclassified to current earnings should the hedges&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;longer be considered effective. The Company expects the hedges to remain fully effective during the remaining term of the swaps.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company previously entered into <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144275121">two</span>&#160;forward starting interest rate cap spread transactions, <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> with a total notional amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144275123" contextRef="i_2022-10-01_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateCapMember_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-CashFlowHedgingMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeLiabilityNotionalAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">150</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, which became&#160;effective on <em style="font: inherit;"> October 1, 2022 </em>and which matures in <em style="font: inherit;"> October </em>of <em style="font: inherit;">2027</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> interest rate cap spread transaction, with a total notional amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144275126" contextRef="i_2022-11-30_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateCapMember_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-CashFlowHedgingMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeLiabilityNotionalAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">75</ix:nonFraction> million, which became effective in <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2022 </em>and which matures in <em style="font: inherit;"> November </em>of <em style="font: inherit;">2027.</em>&#160;These are designated as cash flow hedges of brokered certificates of deposit, and the interest rate cap spread is indexed to a benchmark of fed funds with payment required&#160;on a monthly basis. The structure of these instruments is such that the Company entered into a total of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c144275128" contextRef="i_2022-12-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateCapMember_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-CashFlowHedgingMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember_PositionAxis-ShortMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeLiabilityNotionalAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">225</ix:nonFraction> million in notional amount of sold interest rate cap agreements, in which we are required to pay the counterparty an incremental amount if the index rate exceeds a set cap rate. Simultaneously, the Company purchased a total of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144275129" contextRef="i_2022-12-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateCapMember_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-CashFlowHedgingMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember_PositionAxis-LongMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeLiabilityNotionalAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">225</ix:nonFraction> million notional amount of interest rate cap agreements in which we receive an incremental amount if the index rate is above a set cap rate.&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">No</em> payments are required if the index rate is&#160;at, or below, the cap rate on the sold or purchased interest rate cap agreements.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Interest income&#160;recorded on these swap and interest rate cap transactions totaled approximately&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c144275131" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateCapMember_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-CashFlowHedgingMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestIncomeExpenseNet" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c144275132" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-InterestRateCapMember_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-CashFlowHedgingMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestIncomeExpenseNet" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">4.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million&#160;during the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2025</em>, respectively, and is recorded as a component of either interest expense on FHLB advances or on brokered certificates of deposit.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 0pt;"><b>Derivatives</b>&#160;<b><em style="font: inherit;">Not</em> Designated as Hedges</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">As part of the merger with FLIC, the Bank acquired interest rate swap agreements (each, a &#8220;back-to-back swap&#8221;) that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> designated as hedging instruments. A&#160;back-to-back swap allows a&#160;borrower to effectively convert a variable rate loan to a fixed rate. The Bank originates a variable rate loan with a borrower and simultaneously enters&#160;into offsetting back-to-back swaps&#160;with the borrower and an unaffiliated dealer counterparty to minimize interest rate risk. In connection with each swap transaction, the Bank agrees to pay interest to the borrower on a notional amount at a variable interest rate and receives interest from the borrower on a similar notional amount at a fixed interest rate. Concurrently, the Bank agrees to pay the dealer counterparty the same fixed interest rate on the same notional amount and receives the same variable interest rate on the same notional amount. Because the Bank acts as an intermediary for its borrower, changes in the fair value of the underlying derivative contracts offset each other and do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> impact the Bank&#8217;s results of operations.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The majority of these loans are associated with multifamily properties located in the <em style="font: inherit;">five</em> boroughs of New York City, most of which are entirely or predominantly rent-regulated. This specific pool is subject to unique stressors, primarily due to the <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> New York rent laws, which restricted rent increases while operating in an environment of escalating expenses.&#160;In addition, the current city administration has supported a rent freeze on rent stabilized apartments, while proposing other policy initiatives which could have an adverse impact on rent stabilized properties.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Credit Quality Indicators</span></b> - The Company continuously monitors the credit quality of its loans receivable. In addition to its internal monitoring, the Company utilizes the services of a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party loan review firm to periodically validate the credit quality of its loans receivable on a sample basis. Credit quality is monitored by reviewing certain credit quality indicators. Assets classified as &#8220;Pass&#8221; are deemed to possess average to superior credit quality, requiring <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> more than normal attention. Assets classified as &#8220;Special Mention&#8221; have generally acceptable credit quality yet possess higher risk characteristics/circumstances than satisfactory assets. Such conditions include strained liquidity, slow pay, stale financial statements, or other conditions that require more stringent attention from the lending staff. These conditions, if <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> corrected, <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>weaken the credit&#160;quality or inadequately protect the Company&#8217;s credit position at some future date. Assets are classified&#160;as "Substandard&#8221; if the asset has a well-defined weakness that requires management&#8217;s attention to a greater degree than for loans classified as special mention. Such weakness, if left uncorrected, could possibly result in the compromised ability of the loan to perform to contractual requirements. An asset is classified as &#8220;Doubtful&#8221; if it is inadequately protected by the net worth and/or paying capacity of the obligor or of the collateral, if any, that secures the obligation. Assets classified as doubtful include assets for which there is a &#8220;distinct possibility&#8221; that a degree of loss will occur if the inadequacies are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> corrected.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 27pt;">There were <ix:nonFraction id="c144275251" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="cnob:FinancingReceivableNumberOfModifications" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="INF">eight</ix:nonFraction>&#160;modifications to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty during the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">31,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2026.</em>&#160;There were <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> modifications to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty during the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2025.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 27pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 27pt;">During the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2025</em>, the Company had&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c144275258" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LoansAndLeasesReceivableImpairedCommitmentToLend" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction>&#160;commitments to lend additional funds to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty for which the Company modified the terms of the loans in the form of principal forgiveness, an interest rate reduction, an other-than-insignificant payment delay, or a term extension during the current period.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 27pt;">There were <ix:nonFraction id="c144275259" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis-ConsumerPortfolioSegmentMember_LoanRestructuringModificationAxis-PeriodicPaymentReductionMember" unitRef="Pure" name="cnob:FinancingReceivableModifiedSubsequentDefaultNumberOfContracts" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> loans&#160;to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty that had a payment default during the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2025, </em>which were&#160;modified in the <em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em> months prior to that default. Default is determined at <em style="font: inherit;">90</em> or more days past due, upon charge-off, or upon foreclosure. Modified loans in default are individually evaluated for the ACL&#160;or if the modified loan is deemed uncollectible, the loan, or a portion of the loan, is written off and the ACL&#160;is adjusted accordingly.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">6.</em> Loans and the Allowance for Credit Losses </b>&#8211;<b> (continued)</b></p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 9pt;"><b style="font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Allowance for Credit Losses for Unfunded Commitments</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company has recorded an ACL for unfunded credit commitments, which was recorded in other liabilities. The provision is recorded within the provision for credit losses on the Company&#8217;s income statement.   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock" id="c3175173" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">7.</em> Fair Value Measurements and Fair Value of Financial Instruments</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Fair value is the exchange price that would be received for an asset or paid to transfer a liability (exit price) in the principal or most advantageous market for the asset or liability in an orderly transaction between market participants on the measurement date.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">FASB ASC <em style="font: inherit;">820</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10,</em> &#8220;Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures&#8221;, is the standard used to govern disclosures related to fair value measurements.&#160;FASB ASC <em style="font: inherit;">820</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">05</em> defines fair value, establishes a framework for measuring fair value, establishes a <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>-level valuation hierarchy for disclosure of fair value measurements and enhances disclosure requirements for fair value measurements. The valuation hierarchy is based upon the transparency of inputs to the valuation of an asset or liability as of the measurement date.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">FASB ASC <em style="font: inherit;">820</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">65</em> provides additional guidance for estimating fair value in accordance with FASB ASC <em style="font: inherit;">820</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">05</em> when the volume and level of activity for the asset or liability have significantly decreased. This ASC also includes guidance on identifying circumstances that indicate a transaction is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> orderly.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">FASB ASC <em style="font: inherit;">820</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">05</em> establishes a fair value hierarchy that prioritizes the inputs to valuation methods used to measure fair value. The hierarchy gives the highest priority to unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities (Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> measurements) and the lowest priority to unobservable inputs (Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> measurements). The <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> levels of the fair value hierarchy under FASB ASC <em style="font: inherit;">820</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">05</em> are as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="width: 72pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 45pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i>Level <em style="font: inherit;">1:</em></i></td><td style="width: auto; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">Unadjusted quoted prices in active markets that are accessible at the measurement date for identical, unrestricted assets or liabilities.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="width: 72pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 45pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i>Level <em style="font: inherit;">2:</em></i></td><td style="width: auto; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">Quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities in active markets, and inputs that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly, for substantially the full term of the financial instrument.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="width: 72pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 45pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i>Level <em style="font: inherit;">3:</em></i></td><td style="width: auto; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">Prices or valuation techniques that require inputs that are both significant to the fair value measurement and unobservable (for example, supported with little or <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> market activity).</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The level of an asset or liability&#160;within the fair value hierarchy is based on the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value measurement. The following information should <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be interpreted as an estimate of the fair value of the entire Company since a fair value calculation is only provided for a limited portion of the Company&#8217;s assets and liabilities. Due to a wide range of valuation techniques and the degree of subjectivity used in making the estimates, comparisons between the Company&#8217;s disclosures and those of other companies <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be meaningful.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">7.</em> Fair Value Measurements and Fair Value of Financial Instruments </b>&#8211;<b> (continued)</b></p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><b>Assets and Liabilities Measured at Fair Value on a Recurring Basis</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The following methods and assumptions were used to estimate the fair values of the Company&#8217;s assets measured at fair value on a recurring basis as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Available-for-Sale Securities and Equity Securities</span>: Where quoted prices are available in an active market, securities are classified within Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> of the valuation hierarchy. Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> inputs include securities that have quoted prices in active markets for identical assets. If quoted market prices are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available, then fair values are estimated by using pricing models, quoted prices of securities with similar characteristics, or discounted cash flows. Examples of instruments which would generally be classified within Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> of the valuation hierarchy include municipal bonds and certain agency collateralized mortgage obligations. In certain cases where there is limited activity in the market for a particular instrument, assumptions must be made to determine the fair value of the instruments and these are classified as Level <em style="font: inherit;">3.</em> When measuring fair value, the valuation techniques available under the market approach, income approach and/or cost approach are used. The Company&#8217;s evaluations are based on market data and the Company employs combinations of these approaches for its valuation methods depending on the asset class.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Derivatives</span>: The fair value of derivatives is based on valuation models using observable market data as of the measurement date (Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em>). Our derivatives are traded in an over-the-counter market where quoted market prices are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> always available. Therefore, the fair values of derivatives are determined using quantitative models that utilize multiple market inputs. The inputs will vary based on the type of derivative, but could include interest rates, prices and indices to generate continuous yield or pricing curves, prepayment rate, and volatility factors to value the position. The majority of market inputs are actively quoted and can be validated through external sources, including brokers, market transactions and <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party pricing services.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">There were <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> transfers between Level <em style="font: inherit;">1,</em>&#160;Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> and Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> during the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> and for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>.</p>
