   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -36pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b>Assets Measured at Fair Value on a Nonrecurring Basis</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be required periodically to measure certain assets at fair value on a nonrecurring basis in accordance with&#160;GAAP. These adjustments to fair value usually result from the application of lower of cost or fair value accounting or impairment write-downs of individual assets. The following methods and assumptions were used to estimate the fair values of the Company&#8217;s assets measured at fair value on a nonrecurring basis as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Loans Held-for-Sale</span>: Residential mortgage and SBA loans, originated and intended for sale in the secondary market, are carried at the lower of aggregate cost or estimated fair value as determined by outstanding commitments from investors. For these loans originated and intended for sale, gains and losses on loan sales (sale proceeds minus carrying value) are recorded in other income and direct loan origination costs and fees are deferred at origination of the loan and are recognized in other income upon sale of the loan. Management obtains quotes or bids on all or parts of these loans directly from the purchasing financial institutions (Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em>).&#160;As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;loans held-for-sale totaled $<ix:nonFraction id="c144276529" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_FairValueByFairValueHierarchyLevelAxis-FairValueInputsLevel2Member_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis-SbaLoansMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LoansReceivableHeldForSaleAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">10.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;consisting entirely of SBA loans. As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, loans held-for-sale totaled $<ix:nonFraction id="c144276530" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_FinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis-ResidentialPortfolioSegmentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LoansReceivableHeldForSaleAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, consisting entirely of residential mortgage loans.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">7.</em> Fair Value Measurements and Fair Value of Financial Instruments </b>&#8211;&#160;<b>(continued)</b></p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Collateral Dependent Loans</span>: The Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>record adjustments to the carrying value of loans based on fair value measurements, generally as partial charge-offs of the uncollectible portions of these loans. These adjustments also include certain impairment amounts for collateral dependent loans calculated in accordance with GAAP.&#160;Impairment amounts are generally based on the fair value of the underlying collateral supporting the loan and, as a result, the carrying value of the loan less the calculated impairment amount applicable to that loan does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily represent the fair value of the loan. Real estate collateral is valued using independent appraisals or other indications of value based on recent comparable sales of similar properties or assumptions generally observable by market participants. However, due to the substantial judgment applied and limited volume of activity as compared to other assets, fair value is based on Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> inputs. Estimates of fair value used for collateral supporting commercial loans generally are based on assumptions <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> observable in the marketplace and are also based on Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> inputs.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">7.</em> Fair Value Measurements and Fair Value of Financial Instruments </b>&#8211;&#160;<b>(continued)</b></p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The fair value of commitments to originate loans is estimated using the fees currently charged to enter into similar agreements, taking into account the remaining terms of the agreements and the present creditworthiness of the counterparties. For fixed-rate loan commitments, fair value also considers the difference between current levels of interest rates and the committed rates. The fair values of letters of credit and lines of credit are based on fees currently charged for similar agreements or on the estimated cost to terminate or otherwise settle the obligations with the counterparties at the reporting date. The fair value of commitments to originate loans is immaterial and <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> included in the tables above.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Changes in assumptions or estimation methodologies <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>have a material effect on these estimated fair values.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company&#8217;s remaining assets and liabilities, which are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> considered financial instruments, have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been valued differently than has been customary with historical cost accounting. <em style="font: inherit;">No</em> disclosure of the relationship value of the Company&#8217;s core deposit base is required by FASB ASC <em style="font: inherit;">825</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Fair value estimates are based on existing balance sheet financial instruments, without attempting to estimate the value of anticipated future business and the value of assets and liabilities that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> considered financial instruments. For example, there are certain significant assets and liabilities that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> considered financial assets or liabilities, such as deferred taxes, premises and equipment, and goodwill. In addition, the tax ramifications related to the realization of the unrealized gains and losses can have a significant effect on fair value estimates and have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been considered in the estimates.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Management believes that reasonable comparability between financial institutions <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be likely, due to the wide range of permitted valuation techniques and numerous estimates which must be made, given the absence of active secondary markets for many of the financial instruments. This lack of uniform valuation methodologies also introduces a greater degree of subjectivity to these estimated fair values.</p>
  </ix:nonNumeric>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">8.</em> Comprehensive&#160;Income</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Total comprehensive income includes all changes in equity during a period from transactions and other events and circumstances from non-owner sources. The Company&#8217;s OCI&#160;is comprised of unrealized holding gains and losses on available-for-sale securities, unrealized gains and losses on cash flow hedges, obligations for defined benefit pension plan and an adjustment to reflect the curtailment of the Company&#8217;s defined benefit pension plan, each net of taxes.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">9.</em></b>&#160;<b>Stock-based Compensation</b>&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company&#8217;s stockholders approved the <em style="font: inherit;">2017</em> Equity Compensation Plan (&#8220;the Plan&#8221;) on <em style="font: inherit;"> May 23, 2017.&#160;</em>The Plan eliminates all remaining issuable shares under previous plans and is the only outstanding plan as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>. On <em style="font: inherit;"> May 30, 2023, </em>the Company's stockholders approved an amendment to the Plan that increased&#160;the maximum number&#160;of shares issuable to&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c144276980" contextRef="i_2017-05-23_PlanNameAxis-The2017EquityCompensationPlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,200,000</ix:nonFraction>. Grants under the Plan can be in the form of stock options (qualified or non-qualified), restricted shares, deferred&#160;stock&#160;units or performance units. Shares available for grant and issuance under the Plan as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;were&#160;approximately&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c144276981" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAvailableForGrant" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">64,787</ix:nonFraction>. The Company intends to issue all shares under the Plan in the form of newly issued shares.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>the Company had <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144276982"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144277017">no</span></span> outstanding stock options. Restricted stock and deferred stock units generally vest over a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144276983">three</span>-year period, with <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144276984">one</span>-<em style="font: inherit;">third</em> vesting annually beginning <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year after the grant date. These awards also provide for accelerated vesting upon a change in control. Grants to new employees and board members <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>feature shorter vesting schedules. Performance units typically feature a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144276987">three</span>-year cliff vesting or accelerate upon a change of control. The Company accounts for forfeitures as they occur by reversing previously recognized compensation expense. Restricted stock grants carry the same dividend and voting rights as common stock, while options, performance units, and deferred stock units&#160;do <em style="font: inherit;">not.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">All awards are issued at the fair value of the underlying shares on&#160;the grant date. The Company expenses the cost of the awards, which is determined to be the fair market value of the awards at the date of grant, ratably, over the vesting or measurement period. Forfeiture rates are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> estimated but are recorded as incurred.&#160;Stock-based compensation expense for the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>&#160;months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2025</em> was $<ix:nonFraction id="c144276991" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c144276992" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, respectively.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">Activity in the Company&#8217;s restricted&#160;stock for the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> was as follows:</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 0pt;"><b><i>&#160; &#160; &#160; &#160; &#160; &#160; &#160; &#160; </i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 45pt;"><b><i>Contributions </i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;The Company did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> contribute to the pension&#160;plans during the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>. The Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> plan on contributing amounts to either Pension Trust for the remainder of <em style="font: inherit;">2026.</em> Each&#160;trust is established to provide retirement and other benefits for eligible employees and their beneficiaries under each plan. <em style="font: inherit;">No</em> part of the trust assets <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be applied to any purpose other than providing benefits under the plan and for defraying expenses of administering the plan and the trust.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -38pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b><i>&#160; &#160; &#160; &#160; &#160; &#160; &#160; &#160; FLIC Merger</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 45pt;">In the FLIC merger, the Company acquired a defined benefit pension plan with a net funded status of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144277073" contextRef="i_2025-06-01_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanFundedStatusOfPlan" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">11.2</ix:nonFraction> million as of the Acquisition Date. Former FLIC employees were eligible to participate in the Pension Plan after attaining <ix:nonFraction id="c144277074" contextRef="i_2025-06-01_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="Pure" name="cnob:DefinedBenefitPlanMinimumAgeOfEmployee" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">21</ix:nonFraction> years of age and completing <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-06-01_2025-06-01_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" name="cnob:DefinedBenefitPlanMinimumService" id="c144277075" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">12</ix:nonNumeric> full months of service. Pension benefits are generally based on a percentage of average annual compensation during the period of creditable service. The Bank has historically made&#160;contributions to the Pension Plan which, when taken together with participant contributions equal to <ix:nonFraction id="c144277076" contextRef="d_2025-06-01_2025-06-01_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="Pure" name="cnob:DefinedBenefitPlanEmployerMatchingContributionPercentOfEmployeesGrossPay" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">2</ix:nonFraction>% of their compensation, will be sufficient to fund these benefits. The Bank&#8217;s funding method, the unit credit actuarial cost method, is consistent with the funding requirements of applicable federal laws and regulations which set forth both minimum required and maximum tax-deductible contributions. Employees became fully vested after <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144277077">four</span> years&#160;of participation in the Pension Plan (<em style="font: inherit;">no</em> vesting occurs during the <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c144277079">four</span>-year period). An internal management committee oversees the affairs of the pension plan and acts as named fiduciary.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 45pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Effective <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025, </em>the Company froze benefit accruals under this&#160;defined benefit pension plan for all participants. The freeze does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> affect retirees or vested benefits. The projected benefit obligation was remeasured using a discount rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c144277081" contextRef="i_2025-09-30_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanAssumptionsUsedCalculatingBenefitObligationDiscountRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">5.41</ix:nonFraction>%, increasing the liability by $<ix:nonFraction id="c144277082" contextRef="d_2025-09-30_2025-09-30_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanBenefitObligationPeriodIncreaseDecrease" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">2.0</ix:nonFraction> million. There were <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> other changes in assumptions. The freezing of the plan also resulted in the removal of projected salary increase from the liability determination, resulting in a curtailment gain of $<ix:nonFraction id="c144277084" contextRef="d_2025-07-01_2025-09-30_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanCurtailments" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5" sign="-">3.5</ix:nonFraction> million recognized in other income during the <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2025.</em> The plan&#8217;s funded status improved to <ix:nonFraction id="c144277087" contextRef="i_2025-09-30_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis-FirstOfLongIslandCorporationMember_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-PensionPlansDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanFundedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">134</ix:nonFraction>%.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

All FHLB advances bear fixed rates. The advances as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em> were primarily collateralized by approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c144277135" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FederalHomeLoanBankAdvancesGeneralDebtObligationsDisclosuresCollateralPledged1" scale="9" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">3.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion of commercial mortgage loans and securities, net of required over collateralization amounts, under a blanket lien arrangement. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026,&#160;</em>the Company had a remaining borrowing capacity of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c144277136" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FederalHomeLoanBankAdvancesGeneralDebtObligationsDisclosuresAmountOfAvailableUnusedFunds" scale="9" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">1.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion at FHLB.&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">13.</em> Subordinated Debentures</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">During <em style="font: inherit;">2003,</em> the Company formed a statutory business trust, which exists for the exclusive purpose of (i) issuing Trust Securities representing undivided beneficial interests in the assets of the Trust; (ii) investing the gross proceeds of the Trust securities in junior subordinated deferrable interest debentures (subordinated debentures) of the Company; and (iii) engaging in only those activities necessary or incidental thereto. On <em style="font: inherit;"> December 19, 2003, </em>Center Bancorp Statutory Trust II, a statutory business trust and wholly-owned subsidiary of the Parent Corporation issued $<ix:nonFraction id="c144277177" contextRef="i_2003-12-19_LegalEntityAxis-CenterBancorpStatutoryTrustIIMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-SubordinatedDebtMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentFaceAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">5.0</ix:nonFraction> million of MMCapS capital securities to investors due on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 23, 2034. </em>The capital securities presently qualify as Tier I capital. The trust loaned the proceeds of this offering to the Company and received in exchange $<ix:nonFraction id="c144277178" contextRef="d_2003-12-01_2003-12-31_LegalEntityAxis-CenterBancorpStatutoryTrustIIMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-SubordinatedDebtMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfDebt" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">5.2</ix:nonFraction> million of the Parent Corporation&#8217;s subordinated debentures. The subordinated debentures are redeemable in whole or in part prior to maturity. Upon the cessation of publication of LIBOR rates and pursuant to the Federal LIBOR Act and Federal Reserve regulations implementing the Act,&#160;the&#160;MMCapS capital securities converted effective <em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2023&#160;</em>to a new index based on CME Term SOFR, as defined in the LIBOR Act, plus a tenor spread adjustment, which is referred to as the Benchmark Replacement. Therefore, effective&#160;for quarterly interest rate resets after&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> July 3, 2023 </em>the subordinated&#160;debentures&#8217;&#160;floating rate will be <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>-month CME Term SOFR plus <ix:nonFraction id="c144277180" contextRef="d_2003-12-01_2003-12-31_LegalEntityAxis-CenterBancorpStatutoryTrustIIMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-SubordinatedDebtMember_VariableRateAxis-LIBORLondonInterbankOfferedRateMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">2.85</ix:nonFraction>% plus a tenor spread adjustment of <ix:nonFraction id="c144277181" contextRef="d_2023-07-03_2023-07-03_LegalEntityAxis-CenterBancorpStatutoryTrustIIMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-SubordinatedDebtMember_VariableRateAxis-TenorSpreadAdjustmentMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="7">0.26161</ix:nonFraction>%. The rate as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>&#160;was <ix:nonFraction id="c144277182" contextRef="i_2026-03-31_LegalEntityAxis-CenterBancorpStatutoryTrustIIMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-SubordinatedDebtMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateEffectivePercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">6.78</ix:nonFraction>%. These subordinated debentures and the related income effects are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> eliminated in the consolidated financial statements, as the statutory business trust is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> consolidated in accordance with FASB ASC <em style="font: inherit;">810</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">10.</em> Distributions on the subordinated debentures owned by the subsidiary trust have been classified as interest expense in the Consolidated Statements of Income.</p>

The&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;Notes bear interest at&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c144277190" contextRef="i_2025-05-15_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NotesMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-SubordinatedDebtMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="5">8.125</ix:nonFraction>% annually from, and including, the date of initial issuance up to but excluding&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 1, 2030&#160;</em>or the date of earlier redemption, payable semi-annually in arrears on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 1&#160;</em>and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 1&#160;</em>of each year, commencing&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 1, 2025.&#160;</em>From&#160;and including&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 1, 2030&#160;</em>through maturity or earlier redemption, the interest rate shall reset quarterly to an interest rate per annum equal to a benchmark rate, which is Three-Month Term SOFR, plus&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c144277191" contextRef="d_2025-05-15_2025-05-15_DebtInstrumentAxis-The2025NotesMember_LongtermDebtTypeAxis-SubordinatedDebtMember_VariableRateAxis-SecuredOvernightFinancingRateSofrMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentBasisSpreadOnVariableRate1" scale="-4" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="5">441.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;basis points, payable quarterly in arrears on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> March 1,&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;"> June 1,&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;"> September 1&#160;</em>and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 1&#160;</em>of each year, commencing on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 1, 2030.&#160;</em>Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the benchmark rate is less than zero, then the benchmark rate shall be deemed to be zero.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Operating Results Overview</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Net income available to common stockholders for the three months ended March&#160;31, 2026&#160;was $36.3 million, as compared to $18.7&#160;million for the prior-year period. The Company&#8217;s diluted earnings per share were $0.72 for the three months ended March&#160;31, 2026, as compared with diluted earnings per share of $0.49&#160;for the prior-year period. The $17.6 million increase in net income available to common stockholders and the $0.23 increase in diluted earnings per share were due to a $43.0 million increase in net interest income&#160;and a $2.3 million increase in noninterest income, which was partially offset by an $18.6 million increase in noninterest expenses, a $7.5 million increase in income tax expense and a $1.7&#160;million increase in provision for credit losses.&#160;The increases in net interest income and noninterest expenses were primarily driven by a full three-month impact of the FLIC acquisition in 2026, compared to the pre-merger period in 2025.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Net Interest Income and Margin</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Net interest income is the difference between the interest earned on the portfolio of earning assets (principally loans and investments) and the interest paid on&#160;deposits and borrowings, which support these assets. Net interest income is presented on a tax-equivalent basis by adjusting tax-exempt income (including interest earned on tax-free loans and on obligations of state and local political subdivisions) by the amount of income tax which would have been paid had the assets been invested in taxable assets. Net interest margin is defined as net interest income on a tax-equivalent basis as a percentage of total average interest-earning assets.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Fully taxable equivalent net interest income for the first quarter of 2026 increased $43.4 million, or 65.2%, from prior-year period, due to a 46 basis-point widening of the net interest margin to 3.39% from 2.93%, and a 42.7% increase in average interest earning assets.&#160;The increase in average interest-earning assets was primarily due to the full-period impact of assets acquired in the FLIC merger. The margin also benefited from a 20 basis-point increase in the yield on interest-earning assets and a 49 basis-point&#160;decrease in the average costs of deposits, including noninterest-bearing deposits.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>

    </div>
   </div>
  </div>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Noninterest Income</span></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Noninterest income totaled $6.8&#160;million for the three months ended March&#160;31, 2026, compared with $4.5&#160;million for prior-year-period.&#160;The increase was primarily due to a $1.4 million increase in BOLI income and a $1.3 million increase in deposit, loan and other income, which was partially offset by a $0.4 million decrease in net gains (losses) on equity securities. The growth in deposit, loan and other income&#160;was primarily attributable to the expanded scale of operations following the merger with FLIC.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Noninterest Expenses</span></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Noninterest expenses totaled&#160;$57.9 million for the three months ended March&#160;31, 2026, compared with $39.3 million for prior-year period.&#160;The increase was primarily due to a $10.2 million increase in salaries and employee benefits, a $2.7 million increase in occupancy and equipment expenses and&#160;a $2.6 million increase in amortization of core deposit intangibles.&#160;Other contributing factors included a $0.7 million increase in other expenses, a $0.7 million increase in professional and consulting expenses and a $0.6 million increase in information technology and communication expenses. Additionally, noninterest expenses for the first quarter of 2026 included $2.1 million in merger expenses and restructuring charges, compared to $1.3 million in the prior-year period. Excluding these merger-related items, noninterest expenses would have been $55.7 million and $38.0 million for the 2026 and 2025 periods, respectively.&#160;The variances in nearly all noninterest expense categories were primarily attributable to the expanded operations following the merger with FLIC.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b style="font-size: 10pt;"><span style="text-decoration: underline; ">Income Taxes</span></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Income tax expense was $14.7 million for the first&#160;quarter of 2026, resulting in an effective tax rate of 28.0%, compared to income tax expense of $7.2 million and an effective tax rate of 26.1% for the prior-year period.&#160;The increase in income tax expense and the effective tax rate was primarily due to higher pre-tax income and changes in state and local tax apportionment factors resulting from our expanded presence in New York following the FLIC merger.</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><b>Allowance for Credit Losses and Related Provision</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The ACL is an estimate of current expected credit losses considering available information relevant to assessing collectability of cash flows over the contractual term of the financial assets necessary to cover lifetime expected credit losses inherent in financial assets at the balance sheet date.&#160;The methodology for determining the ACL&#160;is considered a critical accounting policy by management because of the high degree of judgment involved, the subjectivity of the assumptions used, and the potential for changes in the forecasted economic environment that could result in changes to the amount of the recorded ACL. The loan portfolio also represents the largest asset type on the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Statement of Financial Condition.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">As of&#160;March 31, 2026, the Company&#8217;s ACL&#160;was $153.1&#160;million, a decrease of $1.2&#160;million from $154.3&#160;million as of December 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The provision for credit losses, which includes a provision for unfunded commitments, for the three months ended March&#160;31, 2026&#160;and March 31, 2025 was $5.2&#160;million and $3.5&#160;million, respectively.&#160;In each of the quarters presented, the provision for credit losses reflected net portfolio growth, charges related to individually evaluated loans, and changing macroeconomic forecasts and conditions.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -4pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Net charge-offs for the first quarter of 2026 totaled $6.7&#160;million, or 0.23%&#160;of average loans on an annualized basis, compared to $3.4&#160;million, or 0.17%&#160;of average loans, for the prior-year period. The current period activity was primarily driven by the resolution of PCD loans acquired in the FLIC merger, which represented 0.15%&#160;of the total annualized net charge-off ratio.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -4pt; text-indent: 36pt;">These PCD loans were successfully resolved against previously established nonaccretable credit marks and resulted in a $0.2 million release of provision for credit losses upon settlement. Excluding these acquisition-related resolutions, the annualized net charge-off ratio for the originating portfolio was 0.08%&#160;for the three months ended March 31, 2026, a decrease from the 0.17%&#160;reported in the prior-year period.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The level of the allowance for the respective periods of 2026 and 2025&#160;reflects the credit quality within the loan portfolio, expected loan maturity dates, the changing composition of the commercial and residential real estate loan portfolios and other related factors. In management&#8217;s view, the level of the ACL as of March 31, 2026&#160;is adequate to cover credit losses inherent in the loan portfolio. Management&#8217;s judgment regarding the adequacy of the allowance constitutes a &#8220;Forward-Looking Statement&#8221; under the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Actual results could differ materially from management&#8217;s analysis, based principally upon the factors considered by management in establishing the allowance.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Asset Quality</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company manages asset quality and credit risk by maintaining diversification in its loan portfolio and through its review processes that includes&#160;analysis of credit requests and ongoing examination of outstanding loans, delinquencies, and potential problem loans, with particular attention to portfolio dynamics and mix. The Company strives to identify loans experiencing difficulty early&#160;on,&#160;to record charge-offs promptly based on realistic assessments of current collateral values and cash flows, and to maintain an adequate ACL&#160;at all times.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">It is generally the Company&#8217;s policy to discontinue interest accruals once a loan is past due as to interest or principal payments for a period of ninety days. When a loan is placed on nonaccrual status, interest accruals cease and uncollected accrued interest is reversed and charged against current income. Payments received on nonaccrual loans are generally applied against principal. A loan may be restored to an accruing basis when all past due amounts have been collected. Loans past due 90 days or more, which are both well-secured and in the process of collection, may remain on an accrual basis.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 36pt;">As of March 31, 2026, loans 30-59 days past due were 0.81% of loans receivable, compared to 0.19% as of December 31, 2025. This rise is predominantly due to an interrelated series of credits totaling $63.8 million secured by 19 multifamily NYC rent-regulated properties.&#160;We are working with our client to resolve these credits; however, the resulting financial impact cannot be determined at this time.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Nonperforming assets include nonaccrual loans and other real estate owned ("OREO") (the Company had no OREO at the periods presented). Nonaccrual loans represent loans on&#160;which interest accruals have been suspended. In general, it is the policy of management to consider the charge-off of uncollectible amounts of loans at the point they become past due 90 days.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -10pt; text-indent: 9pt;"><b>Purchased Credit-Deteriorated&#160;Loans</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 45pt;">As of March&#160;31, 2026, the Company's recorded investment in PCD loans totaled $207.6&#160;million.&#160;PCD loans, or purchased credit deteriorated loans, are defined by the CECL standard as acquired financial loans that, at the time of acquisition, have experienced a more-than-insignificant deterioration in credit quality since their origination. The Company, with the assistance of independent third-party loan review experts, identified such deterioration by considering various factors. These factors included, but were not limited to, nonperforming status, payment history and delinquency, risk rating, debt service coverage ability, and rate repricing risk. The resulting PCD designated loans include multifamily loans, commercial real estate, commercial loans, and residential real estate.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 45pt;">Within the PCD loan portfolio as of March&#160;31, 2026, there is a pool of rent-regulated loans amounting to $158.0&#160;million. These loans are associated with multifamily properties located in the five boroughs of New York City, most of which are entirely or predominantly rent-regulated. This specific pool is subject to unique stressors, primarily due to the 2019 New York rent laws, which restricted rent increases while operating in an environment of escalating expenses, and certain proposed policies of the new mayoral administration of New York City, including a proposed rent freeze.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 45pt;">Our determination of PCD classification and initial allowance involved significant judgment. Key assumptions included expected remaining life, default rates, recoveries, and economic scenarios. We continue to monitor roll&#8209;off and performance of the PCD portfolio in our quarterly review process.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Investment Securities</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">As of March 31, 2026, the principal components of the securities portfolio were federal agency obligations, mortgage-backed securities, obligations of U.S. states and political subdivisions, corporate bonds and notes, asset-backed securities and equity securities. For the three months ended March 31, 2026, average securities, on an amortized cost basis, increased by $561.3&#160;million to $1.3&#160;billion, or 9.9%&#160;of average total interest-earning assets, from $745.9&#160;billion, or 8.1%&#160;of average&#160;interest-earning assets, for the prior-year period.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">As of March 31, 2026, net unrealized losses on available-for-sale securities, which are carried as a component of AOCI&#160;and included in stockholders&#8217; equity, net of tax, amounted to $48.2&#160;million as compared with net unrealized losses of $40.7&#160;million as of December 31, 2025. The increase in unrealized losses is predominantly&#160;attributable to changes in market conditions and interest rates. Unrealized losses have not been recognized into income because the issuers are of high credit quality,&#160;we do not intend to sell, and it is likely that we will not be required to sell the securities prior to their anticipated recovery.&#160;The issuers continue to make timely principal and interest payments on the securities.&#160;Any impairment that has not been recorded through an ACL&#160;is recognized in OCI, net of applicable taxes.&#160;The Company did not record an ACL&#160;for available-for-sale securities as of March 31, 2026.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Interest Rate Sensitivity Analysis</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The principal objective of our asset and liability management function is to evaluate the interest-rate risk included in certain balance sheet accounts; determine the level of risk appropriate given our business focus, operating environment, and capital and liquidity requirements; establish prudent asset concentration guidelines; and manage the risk consistent with Board approved guidelines. We seek to reduce the vulnerability of our operations to changes in interest rates, and actions in this regard are taken under the guidance of the Bank&#8217;s Asset Liability Committee (the &#8220;ALCO&#8221;). The ALCO generally reviews our liquidity, cash flow needs, maturities of investments, deposits and borrowings, and current market conditions and interest rates.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company utilizes a number of strategies to manage interest rate risk including, but not limited to: (i) balancing the types and structures of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities by diversifying mix, coupons, maturities and/or repricing characteristics, (ii) reducing the overall interest rate sensitivity of liabilities by emphasizing core and/or longer-term deposits and&#160;utilizing FHLB advances and wholesale deposits for our interest rate risk profile, (iii) managing the investment portfolio for liquidity and interest rate risk profile, and (iv) entering into interest rate swap and cap agreements.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">We currently utilize net interest income simulation and economic value of equity (&#8220;EVE&#8221;) models to measure the potential impact to the Bank of future changes in interest rates. As of March 31, 2026&#160;and December 31, 2025, the results of the models were within guidelines prescribed by our Board of Directors. If model results were to fall outside prescribed ranges, action, including additional monitoring and reporting to the Board, would be required by the ALCO and the Bank&#8217;s management.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The net interest income simulation model attempts to measure the change in net interest income over the next one-year period, and over the next three-year period on a cumulative basis, assuming certain changes in the general level of interest rates. The model also utilizes immediate and parallel shifts in market interest rates as of&#160;March 31, 2026.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Based on our model, which was run as of March 31, 2026, we estimated that over the next one-year period a 200 basis-point instantaneous and parallel increase in the general level of interest rates would decrease our net interest income by 4.71%, while a 100 basis-point instantaneous and parallel decrease in interest rates would increase net interest income by 2.73%. As of December 31, 2025, we estimated that over the next one-year period a 200 basis-point instantaneous and parallel increase in the general level of interest rates would decrease our net interest income by 4.95%&#160;while a 100 basis-point instantaneous and parallel decrease in interest rates would increase net interest income by 3.06%.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Based on our model, which was run as of March 31, 2026, we estimated that over the next three years, on a cumulative basis, a 200 basis-point instantaneous and parallel increase in the general level of interest rates would increase our net interest income by 0.10%, while a 100 basis-point instantaneous and parallel decrease&#160;in interest rates would decrease&#160;net interest income by 0.87%. As of December 31, 2025, we estimated that over the next three years, on a cumulative basis, a 200 basis-point instantaneous and parallel increase in the general level of interest rates would decrease our net interest income by 0.32%, while a 100 basis-point instantaneous and parallel decrease in interest rates would increase net interest income by 1.04%.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">An EVE&#160;analysis is also used to dynamically model the present value of asset and liability cash flows with instantaneous and parallel rate shocks of up 200 basis points and down 100 basis points. The EVE&#160;is likely to be different as interest rates change. Our EVE as of March 31, 2026, would decrease by 7.41%&#160;with an instantaneous and parallel rate shock of up 200 basis points, and increase by 0.84%&#160;with an instantaneous and parallel rate shock of down 100 basis points.&#160;Our EVE as of December 31, 2025, would decrease by 7.12%&#160;with an instantaneous and parallel rate shock of up 200 basis points, and increase by 0.28%&#160;with an instantaneous and parallel rate shock of down 100 basis-points.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 5pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The change in interest rate sensitivity was impacted by changes&#160;in overall market interest rates, updates to certain model assumptions, changes in short and intermediate-term fixed rate funding and by the deposit mix shift into certificates of deposit, from both noninterest-bearing and interest-bearing non-maturity deposits.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The following table illustrates the most recent results for EVE and one-year net interest income ("NII") sensitivity as of March 31, 2026.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Certain model limitations are inherent in the methodology used in the EVE and net interest income measurements. The models require the making of certain assumptions which may tend to oversimplify the way actual yields and costs respond to changes in market interest rates. The models assume that the composition of the Company&#8217;s interest sensitive assets and liabilities existing at the beginning of a period remain constant over the period being measured, thus they do not consider the Company&#8217;s strategic plans, or any other steps it may take to respond to changes in rates over the forecasted period of time. Additionally, the models assume immediate changes in interest rates, based on yield curves as of a point-in-time, which are reflected in a parallel, instantaneous and uniform manner across all yield curves, when in reality changes may rarely be of this nature. The models also utilize data derived from historical performance and as interest rates change the actual performance of loan prepayments, rate sensitivities, and average life assumptions may deviate from assumptions utilized in the models and can impact the results. Accordingly, although the above measurements provide an indication of the Company&#8217;s interest rate risk exposure at a particular point in time, such measurements are not intended to provide a precise forecast of the effect of changes in market interest rates. Given the nature and speed with which&#160;interest rates change, the projections noted above on the Company&#8217;s EVE and net interest income can be expected to differ from actual results.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Estimates of Fair Value</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The estimation of fair value is significant to a number of the Company&#8217;s assets, including loans held-for-sale and available-for-sale securities. These are all recorded at either fair value or the lower of cost or fair value. Fair values are volatile and may be influenced by a number of factors. Circumstances that could cause estimates of the fair value of certain assets and liabilities to change include a change in prepayment speeds, discount rates, or market interest rates. Fair values for most available-for-sale securities are based on quoted market prices. If quoted market prices are not available, fair values are based on judgments regarding future expected loss experience, current economic condition risk characteristics of various financial instruments, and other factors. These estimates are subjective in nature, involve uncertainties and matters of significant judgment and therefore cannot be determined with precision. Changes in assumptions could significantly affect the estimates.</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Impact of Inflation and Changing Prices</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The consolidated financial statements and notes thereto presented elsewhere herein have been prepared in accordance with GAAP, which requires the measurement of financial position and operating results in terms of historical dollars without considering the change in the relative purchasing power of money over time due to inflation. The impact of inflation is reflected in the increased cost of operations; unlike most industrial companies, nearly all of the Company&#8217;s assets and liabilities are monetary. As a result, interest rates have a greater impact on performance than do the effects of general levels of inflation. Interest rates do not necessarily move in the same direction or to the same extent as the prices of goods and services.</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Liquidity</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Management actively monitors and manages its liquidity position to determine any current or potential future liquidity needs.&#160;Liquidity is a measure of a bank&#8217;s ability to fund loans, withdrawals or maturities of deposits, and other cash outflows in a cost-effective manner. Our principal sources of funds are deposits, scheduled amortization and prepayments of loan principal, maturities of investment securities, and funds provided by operations. While scheduled loan payments and maturing investments are relatively predictable sources of funds, deposit flow and loan prepayments are greatly influenced by general interest rates, economic conditions and competition.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Liquidity and funding needs are managed through the Bank's Treasury functions and the Asset Liability Committee.&#160;An internal policy addresses liquidity and funds management and management monitors the adherence to policy limits to satisfy current and potential future cash flow needs. The policy includes internal limits, deposit concentrations, liquidity sources and availability, stress testing, collateral management, contingency funding plan and other qualitative and quantitative metrics.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">As of March 31, 2026, the amount of liquid assets remained at a level management deemed adequate to ensure that, on a short and long-term basis, contractual liabilities, depositors&#8217; withdrawal requirements, and other operational and client credit needs could be satisfied. As of March 31, 2026, liquid assets (cash and due from banks, interest-bearing deposits with banks and unencumbered investment securities) were $772.0&#160;million, which represented 5.4%&#160;of total assets and 6.3%&#160;of total deposits and borrowings, compared to $874.4&#160;million as of December 31, 2025, which represented&#160;6.2%&#160;of total assets and 7.2%&#160;of total deposits and borrowings.&#160;As of March 31, 2026, not included in the above liquid assets were securities with a market value of $95.0&#160;million which were pledged to&#160;the FHLB&#160;and securities with a market value of $133.9&#160;million which were pledged to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, which supported&#160;aggregate unutilized borrowing capacity of $215.8&#160;million and $223.3&#160;million, respectively as of March 31, 2026&#160;and December 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Bank is a member of the FHLB&#160;of New York and, based on available qualified collateral as of&#160;March 31, 2026, had the ability to borrow $3.8&#160;billion.&#160;The Bank also has a credit facility established with the Federal Reserve Bank of New York for direct discount window borrowings based on pledged collateral and had the ability to borrow&#160;$2.3&#160;billion as of March 31, 2026. In addition, as of March 31, 2026, the Bank had in place borrowing capacity of $280.0&#160;million through correspondent banks and other unsecured borrowing lines. As of March 31, 2026, the Bank had aggregate available and unused credit of approximately&#160;$4.4&#160;billion, which represents the aforementioned facilities totaling $6.3&#160;billion net of $1.9&#160;billion in outstanding borrowings and letters of credit. As of March 31, 2026, outstanding commitments for the Bank to extend credit were approximately $1.4&#160;billion.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><span style="font-family:'Times New Roman',Times,serif;font-size:10pt;">Cash an</span>d cash equivalents totaled $344.5&#160;million as of March 31, 2026, decreasing by $36.4&#160;million from $380.9&#160;million as of December 31, 2025.&#160;Operating activities provided&#160;$15.3&#160;million in net cash.&#160;Investing activities used&#160;$233.1&#160;million in net cash, a&#160;net increase&#160;in loans $273.3&#160;million and investment purchases of $45.3 million and were partially offset by investment maturities, calls and principal repayments of $89.6 million&#160;.Financing activities provided&#160;$181.3&#160;million in net cash, primarily reflecting a net increase in deposits of $272.3&#160;million and were partially offset by net repayments of FHLB borrowings of $76.0 million.</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Deposits</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 5pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Deposits serve as our primary source of funding. The Company offers a comprehensive suite of products including noninterest-bearing demand, interest-bearing checking, money market, and savings accounts, as well as time deposits with maturities generally ranging from 31 days to 60 months. We supplement core funding with brokered certificates of deposit and internet listing service deposits for asset-liability management purposes.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">To support clients with balances exceeding standard FDIC insurance limits, we utilize reciprocal deposit networks. This primarily includes the IntraFi Network LLC for the placement of Certificate of Deposit Account Registry Service ("CDARS") and Insured Cash Sweep ("ICS") accounts. Through these networks, large-dollar deposits are placed into accounts at other participating banks in increments below the FDIC insurance limit to ensure full principal and interest coverage.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">During the first quarter of 2026, the Company expanded these capabilities by launching a partnership with the National Bank InterDeposit Company (&#8220;NBID&#8221;) network, operated by ModernFi. We are currently in the initial stages of transitioning select client funds to this network to further diversify our reciprocal deposit options. While the financial impact of this transition was not material to our results of operations or liquidity position for the three months ended March 31, 2026, we anticipate utilizing this platform to complement our existing reciprocal programs in future periods.</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Average total deposits increased by $3.6 billion, or 47.0%, during the three months ended March&#160;31, 2026&#160;when compared to the prior-year period. The increase in total average deposits was due to a $1.8&#160;billion increase in demand, interest-bearing and NOW&#160;deposits, a $1.1 billion increase in noninterest-bearing deposits, a $0.4 billion increase in savings deposits and a $0.4 billion increase in time deposits.&#160;The increase in all quarter-to-date average deposit categories was primarily due to the merger with FLIC.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The increase in average time deposits of $0.4 billion during the three&#160;months ended March&#160;31, 2026 was primarily due to a $0.5 billion increase in retail time deposits, partially offset by a $0.1 billion dollar decrease in nonreciprocal brokered certificates&#160;of deposit.&#160;Average nonreciprocal brokered certificates of deposit included in total time deposits were $0.8 billion for the three months ended March&#160;31, 2026, compared to $0.9 billion for the prior-year period.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 27pt;">Average aggregate demand deposits included $1.2&#160;billion and $1.1 billion in ICS reciprocal deposits&#160;during the three months ended March&#160;31, 2026&#160;and March&#160;31, 2025, respectively.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The deposit beta&#8212;the measurement of rate sensitivity in response to market changes&#8212;on nonreciprocal brokered certificates of deposit tends to be higher than that of ICS and CDARS reciprocal deposits. This is because nonreciprocal brokered funds are more directly correlated to prevailing market rates, whereas reciprocal deposits reflect deeper client relationships and a primary focus on FDIC insurance coverage rather than market-leading yields.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Subordinated Debentures</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">During December 2003, Center Bancorp Statutory Trust II, a statutory business trust and wholly owned subsidiary of the Parent Corporation issued $5.0 million of MMCapS capital securities to investors due on January 23, 2034. The trust loaned the proceeds of this offering to the Parent Corporation&#160;and received in exchange $5.2 million of the Parent Corporation&#8217;s subordinated debentures. The subordinated debentures are redeemable in whole or part prior to maturity.&#160;Upon the cessation of publication of&#160;LIBOR rates and pursuant to the Federal LIBOR Act and Federal Reserve regulations implementing the Act,&#160;the&#160;MMCapS capital securities converted as of June 30, 2023 to a new index based on CME Term SOFR, as defined in the LIBOR Act, plus a tenor spread adjustment, which is referred to as the Benchmark Replacement.&#160;Effective&#160;for quarterly interest rate resets after&#160;July 3, 2023 the subordinated debentures' floating rate will be three-month CME Term SOFR plus 2.85% plus a tenor spread adjustment of 0.26161%. The rate as of March 31, 2026&#160;was 6.78%.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 36pt;">During&#160;May 2025, the Parent Corporation&#160;issued $200 million in aggregate principal amount of fixed-to-floating rate subordinated notes (the "2025 Notes"). The 2025 Notes bear interest at 8.125% annually from, and including, the date of initial issuance up to but excluding June 1, 2030&#160;or the date of earlier redemption, payable semi-annually in arrears on June 1 and December 1 of each year, commencing December 1, 2025. From&#160;and including June 1, 2030&#160;through maturity or earlier redemption, the interest rate shall reset quarterly to an interest rate per annum equal to a benchmark rate, which is Three-Month Term SOFR, plus 441.5&#160;basis points, payable quarterly in arrears on March 1, June 1, September 1&#160;and December 1&#160;of each year, commencing on September 1, 2030.&#160;Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the benchmark rate is less than zero, then the benchmark rate shall be deemed to be zero.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><b>Stockholders</b>&#8217;<b> Equity</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The Company&#8217;s stockholders&#8217; equity increased by&#160;$18.2 million when compared to December 31, 2025. The increase in total stockholders&#8217; equity was primarily due to an increase in retained earnings of $27.3 million, partially offset by an increase in the AOCI&#160;of $6.2 million.&#160;As of March 31, 2026, the Company&#8217;s tangible common equity ratio and tangible book value per share were 8.64% and $23.93, respectively, compared to 8.62% and $23.52, respectively, as of December 31, 2025. Total goodwill and other intangible assets were $277.3 million as of March 31, 2026, and $280.2 million as of December 31, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b>Regulatory Capital and Capital Adequacy</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The maintenance of a solid capital foundation is a primary goal for the Company. Accordingly, capital plans, stock repurchases and dividend policies are monitored on an ongoing basis. The Company&#8217;s objective with respect to the capital planning process is to effectively balance the retention of capital to support future growth with the goal of providing stockholders with an attractive long-term return on their investment.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The Company and the Bank are subject to regulatory guidelines establishing minimum capital standards that involve quantitative measures of assets, and certain off-balance sheet items, as risk-adjusted assets under regulatory accounting practices.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;">The following is a summary of regulatory capital amounts and ratios as of March 31, 2026 for the Company and the Bank, compared with minimum capital adequacy requirements and the regulatory requirements for classification as a well-capitalized depository institution (for the Bank).</p>
